reading.body:
Nine political action committees tied to AI and cloud companies gave Pete Aguilar $35,000 across eleven contributions between March 2025 and August 2026, and he voted Yea on every recorded AI bill in the same window.

The money is steady rather than clustered. Amazon's PAC gave twice, in March 2025 and March 2026. Google's PAC gave twice, on the same March 2025 date and again in February 2026. Qualcomm, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir, and Oracle each appear once. The amounts are small and uniform, mostly $5,000, which is the pattern of routine committee giving rather than a single large transaction.

The votes are all procedural. Each is recorded as a motion to suspend the rules and pass, a fast-track procedure used for bills with broad support, so a Yea is not evidence of contested judgment. The data does not name what any of the five bills, H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, S. 146, or the earlier H.R. 7757, actually do. Nothing here connects a contribution to a vote, and the ordering is chronological only.

What this record cannot show is the part that matters most for AI. There is no data on data centers, power contracts, grid interconnection, or permitting in Aguilar's district or committee work, so nothing here speaks to the compute and electricity constraints that shape AI buildout. It covers one member's filings and votes, not the wider pattern, and it says nothing about whether the money changed anything.
